question: GQ-007
subject: the library page, and a data-loss bug my own retention work caused

the_page.built: public/library.html — 78 books, 11,260 chapter headings, 470 KB, client-side search
the_page.why_client_side: public/ is served by a static file server under launchd; there is no backend, and adding one means a process, a port and a failure mode
the_page.what_is_shipped: titles and headings — the table of contents. NOT the 9.8M words of body text.
the_page.served: 200 over the tailnet, verified by fetching it
the_page.linked: from the observatory, verified live — an unlinked page is the same defect one level up

the_bug_i_found_by_running_the_gates.not_from_the_page: from MY OWN retention work an hour earlier
the_bug_i_found_by_running_the_gates.cause: enforce-log-retention.sh refreshes the slice from LIVE before deleting. On its second run the 136 rows were ALREADY deleted, so the refresh rebuilt the slice without them. A projection of a shrinking source is not an archive.
the_bug_i_found_by_running_the_gates.recovery: a full 5.75 GB backup from 2026-08-04T09:19Z still held every row; all four values restored EXACTLY
the_bug_i_found_by_running_the_gates.the_lesson: my safety mechanism destroyed the thing it was protecting, and only an unrelated backup saved it

the_fix.what: the slice ACCUMULATES instead of replacing — keep every row it has, add what live has that it lacks
the_fix.guard: refuses and restores if the row count would shrink
the_fix.proven: artificially cut the slice to 100 rows; the script recovered it to 3,586 and refused nothing it should not have
the_fix.now: 3,620 rows, a superset of both live (3,465) and the backup (2,261)

also_undeclared.free_pages: read 1,153,812 then 1,145,138 then 1,141,436 across three runs minutes apart — a sliding value cannot satisfy an equality check, same as routing.requests
